Content: From the founding of `text(each religion)`, Christians and Muslims shared a belief in

A.Choice: the principle of separation of church and state

B.Choice: the legal equality of men and women

C.Choice: equality of opportunity

D.Choice: a `text(single)` omnipotent deity

Key.Rationale: The founders of both religions, Jesus and Muhammad, drew on the Jewish belief in a `text(single)`, all-powerful deity as the basis of their new faiths, in sharp contrast to the polytheistic religions of the Mediterranean world.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/2a.jpg
The `text(sixth-century C.E.)` Buddhist statue complex shown above, found in China, is an example of

A.Choice: religious conflict

B.Choice: reverence for ancestors

C.Choice: the wealth and power of the emperor

D.Choice: cross-cultural interaction

Key.Rationale: The complex is a Buddhist shrine exemplifying the interaction of Hellenistic, Indian, and Chinese artistic styles. For example, the statues have clothing draped in a Hellenistic style, combined with Indian body poses and Chinese facial features.

Content:
:ibox:“If a [noble] man puts out the eye of another [noble] man, his eye shall be put out.

If he breaks another [noble] man's bone, his bone shall be broken.

If he puts out the eye of a [commoner] or breaks the bone of a [commoner], he shall pay `text(one)` [silver] mina.

If he puts out the eye of a man's slave or breaks the bone of a man's slave, he shall pay `text(one-half)` of its value.”
The excerpt above from the Code of Hammurabi illustrates which of the following about Babylonian society?

A.Choice: It made provision for the economic well- being of all classes.

B.Choice: It moved away from reliance on corporal punishment.

C.Choice: It was marked by social inequalities.

Key.Rationale: The excerpt from the Code of Hammurabi clearly shows a hierarchy in penalties for violence against others. It mandates that those at a higher level of society (noble men) receive less severe penalties for injuries they inflict on members on the lower rungs of society (commoners and slaves) than they receive for injuries inflicted on members of their own level. Thus the law indicates that Babylonian society was unequal.

D.Choice: The king was regarded as blessed by divine forces.

Content: Which of the following contributed significantly to the fall of both the western Roman and the Han empires?

A.Choice: The destruction of overland trade routes

B.Choice: Irregularities in the flow of the silver trade

C.Choice: New military technologies

D.Choice: Invasions by borderland peoples

Key.Rationale: In Europe, Germanic and other peoples posed a severe military threat and ultimately succeeded in ending Roman rule in the western `text(half)` of the empire in the `text(late fifth century)`. In Central Asia, the Xiongnu confederation forced the Han imperial government to spend significant resources on defense, thereby weakening the empire.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/5a.jpg
problems/AP11WH/media/5b.jpg
The graph above shows the effect of which of the following?

A.Choice: The fall of the Roman Empire on population growth

B.Choice: The Agricultural Revolution on food supplies

C.Choice: Plague on the populations of Asia and Europe

Key.Rationale: The most recent research suggests that a serious outbreak of bubonic plague occurred in China in the `text(early 1300s)`, in the wake of disruptions caused by the Mongol conquests. The plague probably traveled along trade routes such as the Silk Roads to India, Europe, and the Middle East. The plague killed large numbers of people in every area it touched, as indicated by the population declines from `text(1300)` to `text(1400)` shown on the graph.

D.Choice: The fall of the Byzantine Empire on population growth

Content: Which of the following describes a major effect of the Bantu migrations?

A.Choice: The spread of Islam across sub-Saharan Africa

B.Choice: The diffusion of iron metallurgy in sub-Saharan Africa

Key.Rationale: Beginning in the `text(first millennium B.C.E.)` Bantu-speaking peoples migrated from West Africa to central, eastern, and southern Africa, bringing with them their knowledge of ironworking. The other answer choices describe events or developments that happened before or after the migrations or were not associated with Bantu-speaking peoples.

C.Choice: The introduction of banana cultivation in East Africa

D.Choice: The success of hunter-foraging in sub-Saharan Africa

Content: Inca and Aztec societies were similar in that both

A.Choice: developed from Maya civilization

B.Choice: acquired empires by means of military conquest

Key.Rationale: Inca and Aztec peoples conquered wide areas and financed their empires by collecting tribute from conquered peoples. Rebellions were dealt with quickly. Military force was the basis of the creation and maintenance of both empires.

C.Choice: independently developed iron technology

D.Choice: depended entirely on oral record keeping

Content: Which of the following changes best justifies the claim that the `text(late 1400s)` mark the beginning of a new period in world history?

A.Choice: The rise of the Aztec and Inca empires

B.Choice: The economic recovery in Afro-Eurasia after the Black Death

C.Choice: The incorporation of the Americas into a broader global network of exchange

Key.Rationale: Prior to the `text(late 1400s)`, the trading networks of Afro-Eurasia, while linked to one another, had no connection to the Americas. The European voyages of the `text(late 1400s)` began the process of bringing the Americas into a global network of trade and biological and cultural exchange. The creation of these interconnections would have profound consequences for the peoples and cultures of the Americas and for the rest of the world. The other options refer either to events that did not occur in the `text(late 1400s)` or to events that are arguably less significant as global turning points.

D.Choice: The emergence of new religious movements in various parts of the world

Content: Which of the following was a major similarity among European colonial empires in the Americas in the period `text(1450)-text(1750)`?

A.Choice: Widespread religious tolerance and diversity

B.Choice: Encouragement of the development of industrial manufacturing in their territories

C.Choice: Enslavement of African peoples and subjugation of Amerindians

Key.Rationale: Colonial empires in the Americas were primarily sources of raw materials and commodities that enriched European countries and investors. `text(Millions)` of Amerindian and African forced laborers mined precious minerals and grew and processed cash crops such as sugarcane and tobacco on plantations in the Americas.

D.Choice: Settlement of `text(millions)` of Europeans in each of their colonial territories

Content: Which of the following European developments is most closely associated with the revolution in Haiti?

A.Choice: The Protestant Reformation

B.Choice: The Russian Revolution

C.Choice: The French Revolution

Key.Rationale: Saint-Domingue (which became Haiti in `text(1804)`) was ruled as a plantation colony by the French. When the French Revolution toppled the French monarchy and eliminated many of the social inequalities in France, many slaves and other people of color believed that the principles of the revolution should be applied to them. The French Revolution was thus an important cause of the Haitian Revolution.

D.Choice: The Industrial Revolution

Content: :ibox:“The yellow and white races which are to be found on the globe have been endowed by nature with intelligence and fighting capacity. They are fundamentally incapable of giving way to each other. Hence, glowering and poised for a fight, they have engaged in battle in the world of evolution, the great arena where strength and intelligence have clashed since earliest times, the great theater where for so long natural selection and progress have been played out.”
The quotation above by an `text(early-twentieth-century)` Chinese revolutionary illustrates the influence of

A.Choice: Social Darwinism

Key.Rationale: The author of the quote is Zou Rong, who agitated against China's Qing (Manchu) dynasty. He uses Darwinian terms-“battle in the world of evolution” and “natural selection” - to explain `text(twentieth-century)` military and economic conflicts between East Asians and Europeans. Darwinian interpretations of history, such as Zou Rong's, often portray international conflicts as a natural consequence of racial characteristics.

B.Choice: communism

C.Choice: National Socialism

D.Choice: anarchism

Content: :ibox:“We shall not repeat the past. We shall eradicate it by restoring our rights in the Suez Canal. This money is ours. The canal is the property of Egypt.”
The quotation above by Egyptian leader Gamal Abdel Nasser (in power `text(1952)-text(1970)`) best expresses support for

A.Choice: communism

B.Choice: liberalism

C.Choice: nationalism

Key.Rationale: The quote most clearly shows the influence of nationalism. Egypt under Nasser's rule rejected Western control of the Suez Canal as an affront to Egypt's territorial integrity. Although the “isms” mentioned in the other answer choices were important ideologies during the period of Nasser's rule over Egypt, the quote does not provide clear evidence of them.

D.Choice: imperialism

Content: Most early civilizations before `text(600 B.C.E.)` shared which of the following characteristics?

A.Choice: Animal herds and portable houses

B.Choice: Large standing armies and elected governments

C.Choice: Urban centers, growing populations, and writing systems

Key.Rationale: Before `text(600 B.C.E.)` early civilizations had developed cities surrounded by permanent, settled agricultural lands, which produced surplus food that in turn supported growing populations. To keep track of food surpluses and other products, most of these civilizations had developed record-keeping or writing systems by `text(600 B.C.E.)`

D.Choice: Caravan trade, underground cities, and large ships

Content: Before `text(500 C.E.)` Judaism and Hinduism were similar in that both

A.Choice: had written scriptures and an ethical code to live by

Key.Rationale: During the `text(final centuries B.C.E.)`, the sacred Vedas were written in Sanskrit. These texts, which had been orally transmitted for many `text(centuries)`, set out ethical behavior for Hindus. Written and oral sources of the Torah probably existed as early as `text(900 B.C.E.)` but were most likely gathered together in the `text(fifth century B.C.E.)` The Torah established rules for living a religious life for Jewish people.

B.Choice: spread widely around the Mediterranean

C.Choice: promoted teachings about reincarnation

D.Choice: advocated a monastic life and a rejection of the world

Content: Between `text(200 B.C.E.)` and `text(200 C.E.)`, the Silk Roads facilitated commodity trade between which of the following pairs of empires?

A.Choice: The Roman and Incan

B.Choice: The Han and Spanish

C.Choice: The Roman and Han

Key.Rationale: Archaeologists have found evidence of trade in luxury goods, such as Chinese silks and Roman glass, though there is no clear evidence of direct political contact between the Roman and Han empires.

D.Choice: The Mali and Byzantine

Content: The development and spread of Christianity and Buddhism before `text(600 C.E.)` had all of the following in common EXCEPT

A.Choice: both were outgrowths of other religions

B.Choice: both were aided in their spread by existing trade networks

C.Choice: the founders of both presented themselves as divine

Key.Rationale: This choice is the only statement that is not true of both religions in their `text(early centuries)`. The Buddha presented himself as an enlightened teacher, though later some Buddhist sects worshipped him as a deity. People who considered themselves Christians did not universally accept the divinity of Jesus until centuries after his death. All the other choices describe similarities between the `text(two)` religions in this period.

D.Choice: both developed monastic orders open to women

Content:
:ibox: “The Crusader states were able to cling to survival only through frequent delivery of supplies and manpower from Europe. [They] were defended primarily by three semi-monastic military orders: the Templars, the Hospitallers, and the Teutonic Knights. Combining monasticism and militarism, these orders served to protect pilgrims and to wage perpetual war against the Muslims.”

	Palmira Brummett, world historian, `text(2007)`

:ibox:“Whenever I visited Jerusalem, I always entered the al-Aqsa Mosque, beside which stood a small mosque which the Franks had converted into a church ... [T]he Templars, ... who were my friends, would evacuate the little adjoining mosque so that I could pray in it.”

	Usamah ibn Munqidh, Muslim historian, Jerusalem, circa `text(1138)`
The `text(second)` passage does not support the `text(first)` passage because the `text(second)` passage

A.Choice: shows that an influx of manpower from Europe was not critical for the survival of the Crusader states

B.Choice: shows that Muslims vastly outnumbered Europeans in the Crusader states

C.Choice: minimizes the importance of Hospitallers and Teutonic Knights in the administration of the Crusader states

D.Choice: presents an incident in which a military order supported a Muslim traveler

Key.Rationale: The `text(first)` passage, from a modern world historian, presents the view that there was “perpetual war” between Christians belonging to the military orders and Muslims in the period of the Crusader states, but the `text(second)` passage, a primary source from the time of the Crusades, shows that friendship and tolerance sometimes existed between members of the `text(two)` groups.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/18a.jpg
The map above shows what significant economic developments?

A.Choice: Trade connections that linked the Hellenistic and Mauryan empires to African cities from `text(300)` through `text(150 B.C.E.)`

B.Choice: Trading networks that promoted the growth of new cities from `text(600 C.E.)` through `text(1450 C.E.)`

Key.Rationale: The map shows trade patterns that persisted in the Indian Ocean basin throughout much of the period `text(600 C.E.)` to `text(1450 C.E.)` This trade encouraged the growth of urban centers along the coasts of East Africa, Arabia, Persia, India, and China, including the ports named on the map.

C.Choice: Chinese dominance of Indian Ocean trading networks because of the voyages of Zheng He in the `text(1400s C.E.)`

D.Choice: Changes in Indian Ocean trading networks that resulted from technological innovations from `text(1450 C.E.)` through `text(1750 C.E.)`

Content: Before `text(1450 C.E.)` which of the following is true of sub-Saharan Africa's commercial economy?

A.Choice: Phoenician merchants controlled most of the long-distance trade of sub-Saharan Africa.

B.Choice: The Mali-Great Zimbabwe trade route dominated the economy of sub-Saharan Africa.

C.Choice: Sub-Saharan Africa exported gold to the Middle East and Europe.

Key.Rationale: Gold and salt were the main commodities traded between sub-Saharan Africa and the Middle East and Europe prior to `text(1450)`. Gold was mined in West Africa and transported across the Sahara to North Africa and from there to Europe and the Middle East.

D.Choice: The Sahara Desert prevented sub-Saharan traders from participating in long-distance trade.

Content: Which of the following consequences of the Columbian Exchange most affected Amerindians in the `text(sixteenth century)`?

A.Choice: Diseases caused pandemics.

Key.Rationale: Amerindians had no natural immunities to Afro-Eurasian diseases such as measles and smallpox. Demographers have estimated that `50` to `80` `text(percent)` of the indigenous population of the Americas died as a result of exposure to Afro-Eurasian diseases, largely in the `text(sixteenth century)`.

B.Choice: Newly introduced crops replaced indigenous American crops.

C.Choice: The influx of African slaves displaced Amerindians.

D.Choice: European livestock disrupted Amerindian agriculture.

Content: The Mughal Empire and the Ottoman Empire before `text(1700 C.E.)` shared which of the following characteristics?

A.Choice: Both empires were able to expand without meeting strong resistance.

B.Choice: Both empires formally restricted foreign trade.

C.Choice: Both empires were ruled by a `text(single)` religious official.

D.Choice: Both empires were religiously and culturally diverse.

Key.Rationale: The Ottoman Empire, ruled by a Turkic-speaking Muslim elite, controlled large numbers of non-Turkic and non-Muslim people. The Mughal Empire, ruled by a Muslim elite of Central Asian origin, controlled large numbers of South Asian and non-Muslim people.

Content: In the period `text(1450)-text(1750)`, which of the following, produced on large plantations by slave labor, were significant commodities in the growing world market?

A.Choice: Grains such as wheat and barley

B.Choice: Tropical fruits such as bananas and oranges

C.Choice: Animal products such as wool and beef

D.Choice: Cash crops such as sugar and tobacco

Key.Rationale: In this period the increased demand for cash crops such as sugar and tobacco led to the creation of a plantation system that produced commodities using slave labor. The profitability of the plantation system led to its widespread use in the Americas.

Content:
:ibox:“The Declaration of the French Revolution made in `text(1791)` on the Rights of Man and the Citizen also states: 'All men are born free and with equal rights, and must always remain free and have equal rights.'

“Nevertheless for more than `text(eighty years)`, the French imperialists, abusing the standard of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, have violated our Fatherland and oppressed our fellow-citizens. They have acted contrary to the ideals of humanity and justice.”

	Declaration of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Viet Nam, `text(1945)`
The excerpt above was written in response to which of the following?

A.Choice: The use of Vietnamese laborers and soldiers by the French in the `text(First)` World War

B.Choice: The end of the struggle for Vietnamese independence known as the Indochina wars

C.Choice: The failure of French colonizers to apply their ideals in Indochina

Key.Rationale: The Vietnamese Declaration of Independence quotes the ideals of the French Revolution. French colonial rulers in Indochina extended few of the rights associated with the French Revolution to colonial subjects. Thus the declaration points out an inconsistency between French principles and French actions in Indochina.

D.Choice: The rapid conquest of French Indochina by the Japanese during the `text(Second)` World War

Content: An important reason for China's rapid population increase in the `text(seventeenth)` and `text(eighteenth centuries)` was

A.Choice: the introduction of new crops from the Americas

Key.Rationale: American crops such as maize and potatoes were adopted in China as part of the Columbian Exchange and led to an increased supply of cheap food. This, in turn, led to a substantial increase in China's population in the `text(seventeenth)` and `text(eighteenth centuries)`.

B.Choice: the end of the bubonic plague in Asia

C.Choice: the widespread adoption of the European `text(three-field)` system

D.Choice: unprecedented immigration from the Mughal and Ottoman empires

Content: Which of the following was a widespread social consequence of industrialization in the `text(1800s)`?

A.Choice: A decline in the social status of women

B.Choice: An increase in the power and prestige of the landowning aristocracy

C.Choice: The general leveling of social hierarchies based on wealth

D.Choice: The creation of a wage-earning working class concentrated in urban areas

Key.Rationale: `text(Nineteenth-century)` industrialization tended to occur in urban areas and was accompanied by internal migration of unskilled laborers from rural areas to cities. This migration led to the creation of a class of urbanized industrial wage-earners. This pattern was repeated in western and central Europe, the United States, and Japan.

Content: Which of the following best describes how `text(nineteenth-century)` European industrialization affected European women's lives?

A.Choice: By the end of the `text(century)`, new social welfare legislation made it possible for most women to earn university degrees.

B.Choice: Married women found it increasingly difficult to balance wage work and family responsibilities.

Key.Rationale: In industrialized areas of `text(nineteenth-century)` Europe, much of the manufacturing work that traditionally had been done by women moved from homes to factories. Married women working in factories could no longer devote as much time to caring for their children and maintaining their households because they had to work away from home in a regimented setting.

C.Choice: By the end of the `text(century)`, women gained the right to vote in most European countries.

D.Choice: Women came to dominate the agricultural workforce as men moved to cities to take industrial jobs.

Content: After the `text(Second)` World War, countries around the world did which of the following to restore the global economy?

A.Choice: Created the European Union to coordinate European economic aid to former colonies.

B.Choice: Developed a common economic aid package for African and Asian states.

C.Choice: Established new financial institutions, such as the World Bank.

Key.Rationale: After the `text(Second)` World War, leaders of the victorious countries recognized the need to establish international financial institutions to encourage stability and economic prosperity. Institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund provided funds for economic development and monetary stabilization. In the `text(years)` following the establishment of these institutions, countries around the world joined them as recipients or contributors.

D.Choice: Allowed the United Nations to take over failing national economies.

Content: Nationalist leaders in Africa and Asia, such as Ho Chi Minh (`text(1890)-text(1969`), Jomo Kenyatta (`text(1894)-text(1978`), and Kwame Nkrumah (`text(1909)-text(1972`), had which of the following in common?

A.Choice: Defense of capitalism

B.Choice: Support for free-trade systems

C.Choice: Rejection of violent revolution

D.Choice: Opposition to colonial rule

Key.Rationale: `text(Twentieth-century)` nationalist leaders in Africa and Asia, no matter what their economic or political ideology, strove to create independent nations in former colonies.

Content: Which of the following statements is true about the world at the end of the `text(twentieth century)`?

A.Choice: The standard of living in the least economically developed countries of the world rapidly approached that of the most developed countries.

B.Choice: The pace and intensity of international contacts accelerated as a result of transportation and communication breakthroughs.

Key.Rationale: By the end of the `text(twentieth century)`, technological innovations had led to the development of the Internet and increased the global accessibility of existing technologies such as television and telephones. These developments made it possible for people around the globe to instantly exchange culture and ideas in ways that previously would have taken `text(months)` or `text(years)`. Continued improvement and expansion of aviation resulted in similar changes in travel.

C.Choice: The world balance of power was reversed as the West no longer had a military advantage over non-Western countries.

D.Choice: World religions were in decline as the spread of science and secularism intensified.

Content: Which of the following best explains why myths are useful to historians?

A.Choice: Myths clarify how ancient technology worked.

B.Choice: Myths analyze how great heroes created the `text(first)` societies.

C.Choice: Myths provide insights into the values and traditions of their societies.

Key.Rationale: Historians often use myths as a source of information about the world views and moral codes of ancient societies, as opposed to the types of information mentioned in the other answer choices.

D.Choice: Myths give detailed plans showing how ancient leaders achieved power.

Content: The development of Indian Ocean trade routes in the period `text(600 B.C.E.)` to `text(600 C.E.)` and the development of transatlantic trade routes in the period `text(1450 C.E.)` to `text(1600 C.E.)` were similar in that both depended on

A.Choice: the impetus of missionizing religions

B.Choice: understanding of currents and wind patterns

Key.Rationale: Knowledge of currents and wind patterns accumulated in both trading regions. Knowledge of monsoon patterns enabled the trade routes in the eastern Indian Ocean to develop in the period `text(600 B.C.E.)-text(600 C.E.)` Navigational tools spread among Arab, Asian, and European societies. Improvements in navigational tools led to better mapmaking, which often recorded dominant ocean currents. Europeans used knowledge to sail farther into the Atlantic, finally reaching the Americas at the end of the `text(fifteenth century)`.

C.Choice: the political consolidation of newly conquered regions into empires

D.Choice: innovations in ship design that originated in Europe

Content: Which of the following best supports the contentions of the world economic theory in the passage?

A.Choice: China was not massively affected by world patterns in the period.

B.Choice: The rise of Protestantism and the Scientific Revolution transformed European cultures.

C.Choice: Latin America exported sugar and silver and imported manufactured items.

Key.Rationale: After `text(1500)`, European states established colonies in Latin America that provided raw materials for export to Europe while importing expensive manufactured goods from Europe. This relationship is a clear example of the world economic theory explained in the passage.

D.Choice: Britain had a relatively weak central government compared to France.

Content: Which of the following statements would challenge the arguments made in the passage?

A.Choice: Strong governments in the slave-exporting regions of West Africa

Key.Rationale: The existence of large empires in West Africa, such as the Songhai during the `text(sixteenth century)`, provides evidence to refute the theory referenced in the question because they are examples of strong governments in areas defined as having dependent economies. The other choices are incorrect because they provide examples that tend to support rather than challenge the theory.

B.Choice: The role of Dutch trading companies in Southeast Asia

C.Choice: The use of slaves and the plantation systems in the Americas

D.Choice: European imports of sugar and tobacco

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/34a.jpg
Which of the following best describes the `text(1936)` lithograph (entitled The Hero) by German artist George Grosz?

A.Choice: A propaganda poster prepared by the Nazi Party

B.Choice: A protest poster against the atrocities of the atomic bomb

C.Choice: A representation of a Holocaust victim

D.Choice: A `text(post-First)` World War print expressing antiwar sentiment

Key.Rationale: The lithograph depicts a wounded `text(First)` World War veteran. The term “hero” in the title is ironic since the veteran is reduced to selling flowers on the sidewalk. The artwork evokes the horrors of the mass destruction of the war and its sad results.

Content: Before `text(600 C.E.)`, large centralized empires, such as the Han, Persian, and Roman empires, extended their military power by

A.Choice: giving more political power to the common people in conquered territories, thus eliminating the need for large armies of occupation

B.Choice: developing supply lines and building infrastructure, including defensive walls and roads

Key.Rationale: All `text(three)` empires maintained transportation routes in their territories, whether with roads and/or canals. Armies and supplies could move quickly to maintain order and information came relatively quickly to power centers. All `text(three)` empires worked to defend their borders in an organized fashion, often using military patrols and barriers.

C.Choice: creating open societies inclusive of different religious and cultural practices, thus decreasing the chance of revolts

D.Choice: recruiting their armies entirely from inhabitants of their core territories and excluding members of newly conquered lands

Content: Which of the following factors represents the most significant cause of the growth of cities in Afro-Eurasia in the period `text(1000)-text(1450`?

A.Choice: Climate change

B.Choice: Increased interregional trade

Key.Rationale: The revival of cities began slowly after `text(1000)` but accelerated after `text(1200)`. The cities of the East African coast became more numerous, large, and prosperous because of their participation in the Indian Ocean trade as the major exporters of African gold. These African cities also shared a common language (Swahili) and culture. Cities of the Delhi Sultanate, the Arabian states, China, and Southeast Asia also grew and prospered from maritime trade. In Europe, Mediterranean cities such as Venice and Genoa expanded their roles as crossroads between Europe and areas to the east - Byzantium, Indian Ocean regions and East Asia. The Hanseatic League, founded in the `text(thirteenth century)` by free towns in northern Europe grew in size and power through its trade in the Baltic region, Russia, and the North Sea area

C.Choice: Decreased agricultural productivity

D.Choice: Increased invasions

Content: Which of the following would be the most useful source of evidence for research about the profits of Portuguese and British slave traders in the period `text(1600)-text(1800`?

A.Choice: Portuguese and British tax records

Key.Rationale: While this choice might seem to be attractive, it would not be as useful a source of information because merchants often failed to report sales in order to avoid paying taxes.

B.Choice: Narratives of slaves transported to the Americas

C.Choice: European slave traders' account books

Key.Rationale: Slave traders' ledgers would provide information about the cost of acquiring enslaved Africans and the revenue generated from subsequent sales, which would make them the most reliable source of evidence.

D.Choice: Journals of African slave traders

Content: The North and South American independence movements of the `text(late eighteenth)` and `text(early nineteenth centuries)` shared which of the following?

A.Choice: Revolutionary demands based on Enlightenment political ideas

Key.Rationale: Leaders of independence movements throughout the Americas were generally influenced by social contract theory, developed by Enlightenment thinkers such as Locke and Rousseau. The theory suggests that governments derive their authority to rule through the consent of the governed and that such authority can be revoked if the government becomes unresponsive to the needs of its people.

B.Choice: Reliance on Christian teachings to define revolutionary demands

C.Choice: Industrial economies that permitted both areas to break free of European control

D.Choice: Political instability caused by constant warfare among the new states

Content: The founding North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is best understood in the context of which of the following?

A.Choice: The Cold War

Key.Rationale: NATO was established as a military and political alliance among the United States and various Western European countries to defend against the perceived threat of the Soviet Union.

B.Choice: The growth of a globalized economy

C.Choice: The establishment of the Nonaligned Movement

D.Choice: The `text(post-Second)` World War population boom

Content: Historians argue that the `text(twentieth century)` marks a significant break in world history for all of the following reasons EXCEPT:

A.Choice: Petroleum use fundamentally changed the relationship of humans to the environment.

B.Choice: The population of the world increased from `1.6` `text(billion)` to `6.1` `text(billion)` people.

C.Choice: Communists established powerful new states in Russia and China.

D.Choice: Low-wage laborers migrated from continent to continent.

Key.Rationale: This choice is the only choice that does not describe a distinctive feature of the `text(twentieth century)`. The large-scale migration of low-wage labor had been part of the world economy since the spread of industrialization in the `text(early nineteenth century)`. The other answer choices are all accurate characterizations of features that do in fact distinguish the `text(twentieth century)` from earlier periods.

Content: Which of the following statements is true about both the Mughal and Ottoman empires in the `text(sixteenth century)`?

A.Choice: In both empires the majority of the people were Muslims.

B.Choice: Both empires had powerful navies that engaged European navies.

C.Choice: Both empires expanded through the use of gunpowder weapons and extensive bureaucracies.

Key.Rationale: The Mughal and Ottoman empires employed advanced military technology, such as guns and cannons, to successfully defeat neighboring peoples who relied on less sophisticated weaponry. Both empires also created bureaucratic systems that facilitated their ability to govern vast territories.

D.Choice: Both empires gave little monetary support to artistic and cultural endeavors.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/42a.jpg
Which of the following about Afro-Eurasian trade is supported by the map above?

A.Choice: The states of the Middle East did not participate in the Indian Ocean trading system.

B.Choice: The Ottoman Empire was located at the intersections of major trading routes.

Key.Rationale: During the `text(early sixteenth century)`, the Ottoman Empire controlled the area around the Mediterranean Sea from the Balkans to Egypt, which gave the empire a strategic advantage within major Afro-Eurasian trading networks.

C.Choice: The Delhi Sultanate relied primarily on sea routes to participate in the silk trade across Asia.

D.Choice: The Islamic states of West Africa maintained close commercial ties with eastern Europe.

Content: In contrast to initial industrialization, the `text(second)` Industrial Revolution in the `text(last half)` of the `text(nineteenth century)` was particularly associated with the mass production of which of the following?

A.Choice: Textiles, iron, and coal

B.Choice: Textiles, automobiles, and plastics

C.Choice: Airplanes, ships, and radios

D.Choice: Electricity, steel, and chemicals

Key.Rationale: The `text(second)` Industrial Revolution refers to the period during the `text(second half)` of the `text(nineteenth century)`, which is characterized by the application of science to industry to create new methods of mass production and technological innovation. The use of electric power, the Bessemer steel production process and chemical industry all developed during this period. The other answers are incorrect because they refer to industries that developed during the `text(early nineteenth)` or `text(twentieth centuries)`.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/44a.jpg
The trend shown on the graph above is best explained by

A.Choice: increased production of cash crops like sugar

Key.Rationale: The plantation economies created in Brazil and the West Indies produced increasing amounts of sugar during the `text(sixteenth)` and `text(seventeenth centuries)`. Sugar plantations increasingly relied on the forced labor of African slaves; thus the increase in sugar production was the primary factor contributing to the expansion of the transatlantic slave trade indicated in the graph.

B.Choice: growth of silver mining in New Spain

C.Choice: industrialized textile mills' demand for raw cotton

D.Choice: African slave-trading kingdoms' demand for European trade goods

Content: Which of the following groups was Bolívar most trying to influence with this letter?

A.Choice: Mulatto shopkeepers

B.Choice: Plantation slaves

C.Choice: Amerindian miners

D.Choice: Creole elites

Key.Rationale: In this letter Bolívar was primarily addressing the people classified as criollos or Creoles. The term Creole in this period referred to people born in Spanish America. Creoles of European descent had higher social standing than did mixed-race groups or indigenous peoples and Africans, but they had lower social standing than did Iberian-born colonists. Creole elites were the strongest supporters of independence movements within the Spanish colonies of the Americas.

Content: Bolívar was describing the effects of which of the following economic policies?

A.Choice: Feudalism

B.Choice: Mercantilism

Key.Rationale: Mercantilism was the dominant economic theory in western Europe from the `text(sixteenth)` through `text(eighteenth centuries)`. Mercantilists saw colonies as valuable for supplying precious metals and raw materials for manufacturing to the colonizing nation while providing an exclusive market for selling the colonizer's manufactured goods. Bolívar proposed that the new nations of the Americas overturn this economic system by developing manufacturing instead of relying on the export of cash crops and raw materials.

C.Choice: Socialism

D.Choice: Capitalism

Content: The expansion of communication and trade networks in Afro-Eurasia from `text(600 C.E.)` to `text(1450 C.E.)` resulted in the spread of which of the following from South Asia?

A.Choice: Military weaponry, such as iron-tipped spears and chariots

B.Choice: Technological and scientific concepts, such as the decimal and `text(zero)`

Key.Rationale: Diffusion of technology and science generally accompanied the growth of Afro-Eurasian trade during this period. Mathematical innovations like the number `text(zero)` and the decimal system originated in South Asia and spread to the Middle East, where they were adopted and eventually spread to western Europe.

C.Choice: Irrigation technologies, such as ceramic pipes

D.Choice: Textile manufacturing processes, such as the spinning jenny

Content: Which of the following is a major difference between the social structures of China and India between `text(600 B.C.E.)` and `text(600 C.E.)`?

A.Choice: Confucianism emphasized spiritual advancement for people who faithfully performed their social duties.

B.Choice: Merchants had the highest social status in India.

C.Choice: Slaves did most of the agricultural work on large Indian estates.

D.Choice: Confucian social hierarchy privileged government officials.

Key.Rationale: In India the system of castes established a social hierarchy that privileged individuals born into castes associated with priestly functions and military duties. In contrast, Chinese Confucian views of social order placed government officials, who were eventually selected by civil service examinations, at the top of China's social hierarchy.

Content: The African proverb, “Until the lions have their historians, tales of hunting will always glorify the hunter,” conveys which of the following?

A.Choice: Common people need to learn how to write so they can tell their story.

B.Choice: Hunting is a sport that brings glory only to the hunter.

C.Choice: The concept of history is much different in Africa than in Europe or the United States.

D.Choice: History usually reflects the viewpoint of the victors.

Key.Rationale: The African proverb quoted expresses the idea that dominant groups generally use their political and economic power to shape narratives of the past.

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/50a.jpg
The map above indicates that

A.Choice: Mali was a major source and hub of the gold trade

Key.Rationale: As indicated by the symbols for gold mines and trade routes on the map, during the `text(fourteenth century)` the empire of Mali controlled the major trans-Saharan trading routes that supplied Afro-Eurasia with gold from West Africa.

B.Choice: Europeans had begun to make inroads in West Africa

C.Choice: Mali remained isolated from Europe and the Middle East

D.Choice: Atlantic ports were crucial for the transportation of salt and gold

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/51a.jpg
The trade patterns shown on the map above depict

A.Choice: British imports of raw materials and exports of finished goods during the `text(nineteenth century)`

Key.Rationale: During the `text(nineteenth century)`, British manufacturers imported raw materials such as cotton from the Americas, the Middle East, and East Asia. These raw materials were then used to produce manufactured goods in Britain that were consumed locally and exported globally.

B.Choice: major slave trading routes in the `text(nineteenth century)`

C.Choice: British trade routes that developed as a result of the disruption caused by the `text(First)` World War

D.Choice: illicit drug routes that developed in the `text(second half)` of the `text(twentieth century)`

Content: Most world historians would agree that the key to European predominance in the world economy during the `text(nineteenth)` and `text(early twentieth centuries)` was

A.Choice: the Industrial Revolution

Key.Rationale: Industrialization gave European states a competitive advantage over nonindustrialized states. Technological innovations in mass production allowed European manufacturers to produce commercial goods and weapons faster and at lower cost than their global competitors could.

B.Choice: European medical technology

C.Choice: Spanish control of New World silver

D.Choice: the Enlightenment

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/53a.jpg
The map above shows which of the following empires at its greatest extent?

A.Choice: The Mongol Empire

Key.Rationale: The map shows the Mongol Empire at its greatest extent during the `text(thirteenth century)`, under the rule of Kublai Khan, when Mongol armies dominated territories in eastern Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and China.

B.Choice: The Russian Empire

C.Choice: The Byzantine Empire

D.Choice: The Ottoman Empire

Content:
:ibox:“I am a griot ... we are vessels of speech; we are the repositories which harbor secrets many `text(centuries)` old. Without us the names of kings would vanish into oblivion. We are the memory of mankind; by the spoken word we bring to life the deeds and exploits of kings for younger generations. ... I teach kings the history of their ancestors so that the lives of the ancients might serve them as an example, for the world is old, but the future springs from the past.”

	An African griot (storyteller), circa `text(1950)`, introducing the oral epic of King Sundiata of Mali, composed circa `text(1400 C.E.)`
The introduction by the griot is intended to serve which of the following purposes?

A.Choice: To establish the griot's authority by connecting him to the past

Key.Rationale: In the introduction, the griot explains to listeners that griots have been traditionally responsible for maintaining their societies' oral history, which serves to legitimize the historical account of King Sundiata.

B.Choice: To exalt the Malian kings above previous dynasties

C.Choice: To highlight the griot's unique abilities as compared to other griots

D.Choice: To portray Mali as a progressive society that is improving on the past

Content: In recent `text(decades)`, many world historians have challenged the commonly held view that Europeans controlled the largest share of world trade in the `text(seventeenth)` through the `text(eighteenth centuries)`.
Which of the following evidence from the period would best support this historical reinterpretation?

A.Choice: Prices for Chinese goods were much higher in Europe than in China.

B.Choice: European trading companies often backed their long-distance trading ventures with the threat of military force.

C.Choice: Asian trading companies dominated trade in the Indian Ocean region.

D.Choice: European merchants transported only a fraction of the goods shipped globally.

Key.Rationale: Evidence of European merchants controlling only a small `text(percentage)` of the total of all the goods shipped across the globe during this period would most clearly challenge the historical interpretation that Europeans dominated global trade.

Content: The United States Declaration of Independence and the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen reflect a shared concern for

A.Choice: physical elimination of the ruling class

Key.Rationale: The concern mentioned in this choice occurred during the French Revolution but not the American Revolution.

B.Choice: confiscation of church property

Key.Rationale: The concern mentioned in this choice occurred during the French Revolution but not the American Revolution.

C.Choice: protection of private property

Key.Rationale: Both documents were heavily influenced by the writings of enlightenment thinker John Locke, who argued that natural law entitled people to the rights of life, liberty and property.

D.Choice: preservation of the monarchy

Key.Rationale: This choice is antithetical to both documents' objectives.

Content: A historian researching the effects of Christian missionaries' activities on local social structures in `text(late-nineteenth-century)` Africa would probably find which of the following sources most useful?

A.Choice: African accounts of converting to Christianity

Key.Rationale: Among the types of sources listed in the answer choices, accounts by African converts to Christianity would provide the best insight into the features of African society that might be altered as a consequence of adopting new religious practices. The other choices provide evidence about the recruitment and funding of missionaries but not about their effects on African social structures.

B.Choice: Fundraising speeches given in Europe by supporters of missionary efforts

C.Choice: Data on the number of missionaries going to Africa

D.Choice: Recruitment advertisements for missionaries in church newsletters in Europe

Content: What was the leading cause of the unprecedented increase in global population in the `text(twentieth century)`?

A.Choice: The end of international epidemics

B.Choice: Global warming and other types of climate change

C.Choice: The impact of medical innovations and public health measures

Key.Rationale: The development of antibiotics and mass vaccination campaigns during the `text(twentieth century)` have had a tremendous impact on global population by limiting the impact of previously fatal or debilitating diseases. Improvements in sanitation facilities in many areas also decreased the incidence of disease, resulting in longer life spans and lower infant mortality.

D.Choice: The reduction of world hunger

Content: problems/AP11WH/media/59a.jpg
problems/AP11WH/media/59b.jpg
Which of the following developments in the period `text(1878)-text(1922` best explains the change in Japanese trade patterns shown in the graphs above?

A.Choice: Japanese manufacturing output decreased because Japanese leaders restricted commercial ties.

B.Choice: Export of manufactured goods declined because United States tariffs on Japanese goods increased.

C.Choice: Japanese manufacturing output rose as a consequence of industrialization.

Key.Rationale: The pie charts reflect the transformation of the Japanese economy as a result of industrialization begun in the Meiji period. By `text(1922)` Japanese manufactured goods dominated Japan's export market. In addition, raw materials to support industry made up about `text(half)` of Japan's imports.

D.Choice: Japanese imports of raw materials increased as a consequence of extensive immigration to Japan.

Key.Rationale: This choice may attract students because it correctly states that imports of raw materials increased but the reason given, extensive immigration to Japan, is inaccurate.

Content:
“What is recorded in the Buddhist scriptures is analogous to the teachings contained in the scripture of Laozi [the founder of Daoism] in China, and it is actually believed that Laozi, after having gone to India, instructed the barbarians and became the Buddha.”

	Yu Huan, Chinese historian, circa `text(250 C.E.)`
In the fictionalized account of the origins of Buddhism outlined in the passage above, Yu Huan's purpose was most likely to

A.Choice: make it easier for his Buddhist readers to convert to Daoism

Key.Rationale: This choice may be true, but it is an unintended consequence of the account and is therefore incorrect.

B.Choice: hint at the existence of an alternate set of Buddhist scriptures that were different from the officially accepted `text(ones)`

C.Choice: demonstrate the extent of missionary and trade links between China and India

D.Choice: assert the superiority of Chinese culture over non-Chinese cultures

Key.Rationale: Yu Huan's account privileges Chinese over Indian culture by incorrectly claiming that Buddhism was introduced into India from China.

Content: Which of the following statements best represents a nationalistic interpretation of the collapse of the Ottoman and Russian empires during and immediately after the `text(First)` World War?

A.Choice: Military weakness and political instability were the primary reasons for the collapse of these empires.

B.Choice: The growing demands of various ethnic groups within these multiethnic empires were the primary reasons for the collapse.

Key.Rationale: The historical interpretation described in this choice suggests that the demand for political autonomy by various ethnic groups within `text(each multiethnic empire)` led to their collapse. Within the Russian and Ottoman empires, the majority ethnic groups had tried to achieve greater political unity by imposing their language and culture on other groups, which in turn had led to greater nationalist tensions. This interpretation emphasizes the role of nationalism, unlike the other choices.

C.Choice: The slow pace of industrialization in these empires left them unable to compete militarily and politically with more developed countries.

D.Choice: Religious differences between the Russian Empire and the Ottoman Empire led to their final collapse.

Content: Which of the following was a major similarity between the goals of leaders of the Chinese Communist Revolution, such as Mao Zedong, and the goals of leaders of the Mexican Revolution, such as Emiliano Zapata, in the `text(early twentieth century)`?

A.Choice: Advocacy of a global workers' revolution

B.Choice: Active encouragement for integration into the global economy

C.Choice: Concern primarily with improving conditions for urban factory workers

D.Choice: Support for redistribution of land to poor peasants

Key.Rationale: Mao Zedong's agricultural reform program and Emiliano Zapata's Plan of Ayala both called for land to be taken from large landowners and given to peasant communities.

Content: Zeng Guofan's analysis of the situation in China in `text(1854)` was likely influenced by which of the following?

A.Choice: The Daoist notion of being in harmony with nature

B.Choice: The absolutist notion of the divine right of kings

C.Choice: The Buddhist notion of avoiding violence against any living thing

D.Choice: The Confucian notion of the dynastic cycle

Key.Rationale: The proclamation reflects the Confucian view that rulers who are inept or unjust will lose power (the mandate of heaven). The passage details the failure of earlier dynasties to reform government in the face of rebellion. It argues that, in contrast, the Qing emperor has instituted reforms and thus should succeed against the Taiping rebels.

Content: In the passage above, Zeng Guofan's purpose in listing the policies of the current Qing emperor is most likely to

A.Choice: demonstrate the similarity between the damage done by the Taiping rebellion to the Qing Empire and the damage done by earlier rebellions to other Chinese dynasties

B.Choice: mobilize popular support by showing that the Taiping rebellion does not represent a legitimate challenge to Qing rule

Key.Rationale: The Qing emperor is portrayed as reforming “misgovernment,” unlike earlier dynasties. His reforms show that he is responding to his people's needs and is following a righteous path. His actions, as described in the proclamation, indicate that he is the legitimate ruler of the Chinese people, while the Taiping rebels are characterized as bandits.

C.Choice: warn that the Qing policies of keeping taxes low and avoiding conscription might come to an end if the Taiping rebellion succeeds

D.Choice: argue that the emperor's personal piety and benevolent rule prove that he accepts the validity of the Taiping rebels' grievances

Content: Which of the following was a significant environmental effect of the globalization of the world's economy in the period `text(1980)` to the present?

A.Choice: There was a significant improvement in air and water quality worldwide.

B.Choice: While air and water quality generally improved in the developed world, they deteriorated in many parts of the developing world.

Key.Rationale: Since `text(1980)` the combination of environmental regulations and a reduction in heavy manufacturing has led to a general improvement in air and water quality in the developed world. In contrast, many parts of the developing world are experiencing greater environmental damage as they become more industrialized.

C.Choice: Emissions of greenhouse gasses that contribute to global warming generally decreased.

D.Choice: While biodiversity decreased in the developing world, it generally increased in the developed world.

Content: Some historians consider the `text(late nineteenth century)` and `text(early twentieth century)` to have been crucial `text(decades)` in the development of Western thought. Which of the following best supports that contention?

A.Choice: Discoveries in physics introduced the concepts of uncertainty and relativity, which challenged mechanistic models of the universe.

Key.Rationale: At the turn of the `text(twentieth century)`, mechanistic models of the universe proved to be inadequate in describing the behavior of matter on the atomic level or when approaching the speed of light. New discoveries in physics provided better explanations for the behavior of matter and encouraged technological innovation and new ways of thinking about the universe.

B.Choice: Christian missionaries introduced strains of relativism into Western thought after encountering cultures with radically different world views.

C.Choice: Efficiency experts employed scientific methods to regulate the workplace and thereby encouraged faith in economic progress.

D.Choice: Visual artists inspired by photography made realism the dominant aim of painter and sculptors.

Content: Some historians have argued that significant social inequalities emerged only after the adoption of agriculture made it possible for some individuals to accumulate great amounts of surplus wealth.
Which of the following most directly `ultext(undermines)` that assertion?

A.Choice: In the few hunting-gathering societies that remain today, men and women often share in decision making concerning the entire group.

B.Choice: Rulers of ancient river valley civilizations, such as Egyptian pharaohs or Mesopotamian kings, often claimed descent from (or affinity with) the gods.

C.Choice: Archaeological evidence from many later Neolithic settlements in the Fertile Crescent has revealed increasing variations among the size of houses.

D.Choice: Some preagricultural archaeological sites across the world have yielded evidence of significant disparities in the amount and quality of objects placed in individual graves.

Key.Rationale: In the absence of written records, archaeological findings, including data from burial sites, form an important source of evidence for Paleolithic hunter-gatherer societies. The disparity in the quantity and quality of grave goods found in some burial sites of preagricultural peoples suggests the existence of social stratification.

Content: Before `text(600 C.E.)`, all of the following were part of the Confucian social order EXCEPT

A.Choice: loyalty to the ruler

B.Choice: filial obedience to one's father

C.Choice: respect for the old

D.Choice: marital fidelity by husbands

Key.Rationale: Nothing in the Confucian system of ethics required that men remain faithful to one wife. Men had multiple wives and/or concubines, depending on their financial means. All of the other answer choices are basic principles of Confucian social order, which emphasized obedience to authority, filial piety, and ancestor worship.

Content: Which of the following accurately describes the Mongol Empire's role in facilitating trans-Eurasian trade?

A.Choice: It imposed Mongol religious beliefs and practices on conquered peoples.

B.Choice: It reestablished the Silk Roads between East Asia and Europe.

Key.Rationale: The Mongol Empire was able to ensure a measure of peace and stability along the Silk Roads through its political control of the surrounding regions. This contributed to an increase in trade across Eurasia.

C.Choice: It created a self-contained economic system by banning non-Mongol merchants from its territories.

D.Choice: It developed a sophisticated bureaucracy staffed by talented Mongols.

Content:
:ibox:“For the sake of the preservation of this entire creation, Purusha, the exceedingly resplendent `text(one)`, assigned separate duties to the classes which had sprung from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet.”

	Code of Manu, circa `text(300 B.C.E.)`
The passage above most reflects which of the following cultural traditions?

A.Choice: The concept of caste in the Vedic religions

Key.Rationale: The passage reflects support for a strictly hierarchical society with separate tasks for `text(each group)`, whose place in society was determined at birth. These ideas are closest to the Vedic religions of India.

B.Choice: The Daoist emphasis on the balance between humans and nature

C.Choice: Buddha's teaching about the search for enlightenment

D.Choice: Confucius' teaching on social harmony

Content: Write an essay that:

:ibox:• Has a relevant thesis and supports that thesis with evidence from the documents.

• Uses all of the documents.

• Analyzes the documents by grouping them in as many appropriate ways as possible. Does not simply summarize the documents individually.

• Takes into account the sources of the documents and analyzes the authors' points of view.

• Identifies and explains the need for at least `text(one)` additional type of document.
You may refer to relevant historical information not mentioned in the documents.

Using the following documents, analyze the effects of the Cuban Revolution on women's lives and gender relations in Cuba in the period from `text(1959)` to `text(1990)`. Identify an additional type of document and explain how it would help analyze the effects of the revolution.

:ibox:`ultext(Historical Background)`: Cuban revolutionary Fidel Castro assumed power after overthrowing the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista in `text(January 1959)`. Castro then began a radical restructuring of Cuban society along socialist lines.
Write an essay that:

:ibox:• Has a relevant thesis and supports that thesis with appropriate historical evidence.

• Addresses all parts of the question.

• Uses world historical context to show continuities and changes over time.

• Analyzes the process of continuity and change over time.
Analyze continuities and changes in labor systems between `text(1450)` and `text(1900)` in `text(ONE)` of the following regions.

:ibox:• Latin America and the Caribbean
• Oceania
• Sub-Saharan Africa
Write an essay that:

:ibox:• Has a relevant thesis and supports that thesis with appropriate historical evidence.

• Addresses all parts of the question.

• Makes direct, relevant comparisons.

• Analyzes relevant reasons for similarities and differences.

Analyze similarities and differences between the diffusion of Buddhism from its origins to `text(1450)` and the diffusion of Christianity from its origins to `text(1450)`. Be sure to discuss how `text(each religion)` gained followers as it diffused.
